questions.q: Explain the concept of the investment multiplier.

answer.text: The investment multiplier explains how an initial increase in investment leads to a much larger increase in national income and employment. When investment rises, it creates income for some people, who then spend a part of it, creating income for others, who spend again, and so on through successive rounds.

Suppose new investment is made in building a factory. The wages and payments made become income for workers and suppliers. They spend a portion of this income on goods and services, which becomes income for shopkeepers and producers, who in turn spend part of it. This chain of spending multiplies the original investment several times over in the form of total income.

The size of the multiplier depends on the marginal propensity to consume. It is given by the formula, multiplier equals one divided by one minus the marginal propensity to consume. The greater the tendency to spend, the larger the multiplier.

answer: Thus a small rise in investment can produce a large rise in national income.
